subject: Information Theory
title: Bit Error Rate
description: A fast breakdown of Bit Error Rate for builders.

hook.text: Wi-Fi operates at a bit error rate below one in a million. Your Bluetooth headphones tolerate one in a thousand.

buildup.text: Bit error rate (BER) measures the fraction of received bits that are wrong. Lower is better.

discovery.text: BER depends on signal strength, noise, and the coding scheme. Error correction codes drive BER down dramatically.

twist.text: Even a BER of 10⁻⁹ means one error every gigabit. For terabyte drives, that's thousands of errors per transfer.

climax.text: Modern systems stack multiple layers of error correction to push effective BER below 10⁻¹⁵.

punchline.text: One in a billion sounds safe. Multiply by terabytes.

quiz.question: Why is a BER of 10⁻⁹ still problematic for large storage systems?
options: At terabyte scale, billions of bits mean thousands of errors
